title: Ghost Docs Sweep — action plan & notes
content:
Meeting snapshot: Ghost Docs Sweep (Jun 29 2026) — quick notes, context, and action plan

Attendees: Anika P., Marcus L., Sofia R., Evan C., Priya N.
Meeting length: 55m (standup-style deep-dive)
Purpose: triage and remove/restore ‘ghost’ developer-facing artifacts — old quickstarts, sample projects, half-finished doc pages, and duplicated HOWTOs that create confusion in the Quickstart surface.

Background/context (why now)
- Multiple incoming support tickets and community PRs referencing stale quickstarts that fail on the new SDK.
- Telemetry: quickstart-run success rates dropped 12% month-over-month; failure spikes correlate with docs last-updated 2024–early-2025.
- Goal: reduce developer friction by a) removing evidently dead artifacts, b) restoring a minimal set of clear quickstarts for v2 SDK, and c) tagging or archiving anything we keep.

High-level decisions from the meeting
1) Conservative deletion policy: do NOT fully delete anything without a 2-week deprecation window and an archive copy in /archive/docs/ghost-sweep (Team will create the archive folder).
2) Triage buckets: "remove", "fix-in-place", "migrate-to-sample-repo", "flag-as-archival".
3) Ownership model: each bucket gets a lead + one reviewer. Leads will make the final call for items in their bucket.
4) Quick wins: prioritize 3 quickstarts to replace within 2 sprints (v2 SDK hello-world, local-runner, and embeddings-minimal).

Triage notes (top-level findings)
- ~45 candidate items surfaced by the grep of docs repo + sample repos; automated script parked at GH PR 842 (see linked artifact).
- Many items are small variants of the same example (e.g., explicit tokenization examples differing only by CLI flags). Recommend consolidating into single canonical example with variants section.
- 7 quickstarts depend on deprecated environment variables (REDWOOD_API_KEY -> REDWOOD_KEY); these must be updated or marked as archived.
- 4 sample apps call internal-only endpoints (private beta) — need to either remove calls or gate them and mark them private.

Action items (owners, rough timeline)
- Anika: create /archive/docs/ghost-sweep and move snapshots of any candidate before action is applied. Due: 2026-07-02.
- Marcus: run the triage script across the docs and produce a CSV with columns (path, last_modified, suggested_bucket, confidence). Share CSV in Confluence. Due: 2026-07-01.
- Sofia: lead "fix-in-place" bucket. Prioritize v2 SDK compatibility fixes, update code samples to use new client APIs, and add a short compatibility note at the top of modified pages. Due: 2026-07-12 (initial pass).
- Evan: lead "migrate-to-sample-repo" bucket. For any runnable sample, move it to github.com/redwood-inference/samples where CI can run quickstart smoke tests. Add GitHub Actions to run on PRs. Due: 2026-07-19.
- Priya: owner for "remove" bucket. Validate low-traffic items, check linked community PRs, announce upcoming removal on #devexp and in release notes. Due: 2026-07-09.
- All: weekly quick sync Fridays 10:30–10:45am PT for status — first sync 2026-07-02.

Criteria for buckets (short)
- remove: not used by any customer/internal sample, breaks on current SDK, no clear owner, <10 page views/month.
- fix-in-place: short patch (<= 60 minutes dev time) to make compatible with SDK v2 and pass quickstart smoke test.
- migrate-to-sample-repo: runnable app that benefits from CI, tests, or environment scaffolding.
- flag-as-archival: valuable historical notes or design rationale — keep but mark with archival banner and disable search indexing.

Edge cases discussed
- Forked community sample that we didn’t author but references Redwood brand: leave in place but add a prominent compatibility blurb and link to supported examples.
- Docs that contain customer PII or client-owned snippets: escalate to Legal before any migration or archive (JIRA: DX-671 assigned).
- Tutorials that depend on Dedicated-only features: convert to "private" label and move to private-deployments doc area, with cross-link.

Quickstart focus (kickers)
- Identify three canonical quickstarts to be the new "starter pack":
  * quickstart-hello-v2 (JS + Python) — minimal token cost, streaming off by default
  * quickstart-local-runner — how to run locally with CPU fallback and a Dockerfile
  * quickstart-embeddings-minimal — embedding request + simple similarity search
- Each quickstart must include: expected setup time (5–7 min), one command to run, expected output snippet, troubleshooting section with one common failure and fix.

Communications plan
- Slack: announce intent + 2-week deprecation list in #devexp on 2026-07-05.
- Confluence: publish the triage CSV and canonical checklist when Marcus shares it.
- Release notes: include a short note for SDK v2.1 release about removed/archived quickstarts.

Notes-to-self / rough heuristics observed
- Many stale docs were last touched by "doc-bot" commits in late 2023 — the automated updates introduced a few regressions when the SDK changed shape.
- Example duplication is worse across sample repos than in docs site; prioritize GH samples migration.
- Small friction wins (fix a single flag in 5 pages) can yield measurable lift in quickstart success metrics; aim for ~10 quick fixes in the first week.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Do we want a short "doc health" badge (green/yellow/red) for each page showing last-smoke-test date? (Idea: show on docs sidebar) — assigned to Sofia to prototype.
- Can we add a server-side redirect for archived pages to an archival index? (Needs infra/console help) — Slack ping infra and file ticket if needed.

Immediate next steps (today / tomorrow)
1) Marcus posts triage CSV to Confluence and shares link in #devexp. (Due 2026-07-01)
2) Anika creates archive folder and skeleton index with README describing policy. (Due 2026-07-02)
3) Sofia picks 5 "fix-in-place" items for the first pass and leaves code comments on the PRs. (Due 2026-07-06)

Reference snippets / thinking
- Example archival banner copy (leave on old pages): "This page has been archived as part of the Developer Experience cleanup (June 2026). The content may be out of date. For maintained quickstarts, see [starter pack link]."

Slack / PRs to watch
- GH PR 842 — initial sweep script + candidate list (owner: Marcus)
- Slack thread: #devexp — message ts:1629456789.000200 (discussion about quickstart failure modes)

If you’re reading this and want to claim an item: drop a comment in the CSV row and ping me (Anika) in Slack.

-- end of notes --

Working draft; will convert to Confluence playbook after initial triage results.
